label: Q-05
title: The new exact-equality quote check is not a slippage or minimum-output guard, yet its comment and error name present it as protection against being short-changed - which risks a future reader believing ledger F-01 has been fixed when it has not
titleNote: RETITLED. The classifier's 'is a tautology on any honest minter' is OVERSTATED and this run's own evidence disproves it - see claimCorrection.
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Newly minted this run; verified to reproduce from fingerprintBasis and not to collide with any of the 19 pre-existing ledger fingerprints. Minted on the NEW function name `annihilate`, which is correct and is not fingerprint drift.

claimCorrection.authority: validity-checker (VALID-IF-RESCOPED, 'rescoping is mandatory, not stylistic') + severity-auditor. BINDING.
claimCorrection.withdrawnClaim: 'The check is a tautology' / 'a no-op on 100% of the honest path'.
claimCorrection.whyWithdrawn: THIS RUN'S OWN EVIDENCE DISPROVES IT. `mintedForStable` is a BALANCE DELTA (Antimatter's phUSD balance after the mint minus the :244 snapshot), NOT the minter's return value. The exact equality therefore DOES catch mid-call phUSD injection: Tier2Delta.t.sol::test_midCallPhUSDInjectionNowReverts reverts PhUSDAmountMismatch(100e18, 100e18+1) when a hooked stablecoin injects 1 wei of phUSD mid-call. The check genuinely closes ledger L-01's donation-attribution gap (and, per L-01's re-wording, converts that gap from a silent mis-forward into a revert). Calling it a tautology overstates in the direction of DISMISSING WORKING PROTECTION, and the pipeline rejects claims a reader can falsify from the repo's own test file.
claimCorrection.correctClaim: The check verifies the minter against its own quote and rejects mid-call phUSD injection, but it is NOT A SLIPPAGE OR MINIMUM-OUTPUT GUARD: both sides re-quote at whatever rate is live at execution, so an owner rate change mid-flight passes the check unnoticed - yet the comment at :232-233 and the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch read as protection against being short-changed.

classification.assetImpact: NONE from the check itself, and the check does real work (it rejects mid-call phUSD injection). The impact it FAILS to prevent is ledger F-01's, unchanged: an owner who lowers exchangeRate while an annihilate is in flight settles that caller at the new rate - 100 AM burned, 100 USDC pulled, 150 phUSD delivered instead of 200 - with the burn already irreversible and no caller-supplied minimum anywhere.
attackPath: 2. PhusdStableMinter.mint computes its own phUSDAmount at PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 by calling the SAME public view with IDENTICAL arguments in the SAME transaction against the same config storage.

3. Because both sides re-quote from live storage, neither an exchangeRate change nor a decimals change BETWEEN the two reads is possible - and, decisively, a rate change BEFORE the whole call is reflected on BOTH sides equally.

4. Owner calls minter.updateExchangeRate(usdc, 0.5e18) while Alice's annihilate(usdc, alice, 100e18) is pending. Alice lands at the new rate and receives 150 phUSD instead of the 200 she saw when she signed.
5. expectedForStable (50e18) EQUALS mintedForStable (50e18) - because the check re-quotes at the NEW rate too - so PhUSDAmountMismatch does not fire and the code reports success.

6. A reader of the comment at :232-233 ('Measuring against its own quote, rather than merely against zero, means a short mint cannot pass unnoticed') and of the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch would reasonably believe otherwise.
whatTheCheckDOESCover: A minter whose mint() disagrees with its own calculateMintAmount() - genuine protection against a future or swapped minter.
Third-party phUSD arriving at Antimatter between the :244 snapshot and the :256 read - PROVEN by test_midCallPhUSDInjectionNowReverts, which reverts PhUSDAmountMismatch(100e18, 100e18+1).
classification.whatTheCheckDoesNOTCover: Anything the caller saw at signing time. There is no caller-supplied minimum-output parameter anywhere in annihilate, so an owner rate change mid-flight is settled at the new rate and the check tracks it rather than resisting it.
classification.likelihood: The framing defect is CERTAIN - the comment and error name are what they are on every read. The mis-settlement the check does not catch has the likelihood already recorded against ledger F-01 and is not re-counted here.
classification.externalRequirements: An owner rate change mid-flight for the uncaught mis-settlement.

faithfulnessNote: Deliberately NOT tagged faithfulness and deliberately NOT collapsed into F-04. This is a defect in what the code's own comment claims, not a deviation from a story - no story speaks to this post-condition at all, which is exactly what F-04 reports. Collapsing them would hide the F-01 tripwire inside a process finding.
c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'function incorrect as to spec, issues with comments'. Squarely the comment/spec limb. It does not reach Medium: the new post-condition is strictly STRICTER than the one it replaced, so it removes no capability, impairs no availability, and leaks no value.
justification: QA is the honest band and inflating it would be overstatement, which the pipeline rejects. But this finding's value is not its band - it is a TRIPWIRE, and it must survive triage as one. The new code now LOOKS like the guard ledger F-01 asked for without being it, and that is strictly worse for a future reader than the guard's plain absence was: a triager comparing F-01's recommendation ('assert mintedForStable against calculateMintAmount') against :234/:257 would find an apparent match and close a live finding. F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060) is 'no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn', and no minimum-output guard exists at c91bc1a - there is no caller-supplied minimum parameter anywhere in annihilate. Note the interaction with F-04: the same untagged commit that over-claims its coverage here is the commit no story authorises. Both point at the same missing review. The standing rule that falsely-exhaustive in-source docs RAISE severity is applied to stop this being culled as a nitpick, not to manufacture impact.

reweighCondition.condition: IF ledger F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060) is ever CLOSED, or IF this guard is ever CITED as closing it, Q-05 MUST BE RE-WEIGHED TO LOW.
reweighCondition.reason: Q-05 is held at QA only because F-01 remains open and independently visible, so the framing defect costs a reader nothing they cannot recover from the ledger. The moment F-01 is closed - or closed ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS CHECK - the misleading comment becomes the ONLY surviving account of what the settlement path guarantees, and the reader has no correction available. At that point it is a Low, not a QA note.

falseClosureBlock.attestationRequiredBeforeClosingF01: F-01 may be marked fixed ONLY on evidence of a CALLER-SUPPLIED minimum-output parameter (e.g. `uint256 minPhUSDOut` checked as `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260). The :234/:257 exact-equality pair does NOT satisfy this and must never be cited as satisfying it: both sides re-quote from the same view in the same transaction, so the check tracks an owner rate change instead of resisting it.
falseClosureBlock.preservedIntactThroughRewording: YES. The claim correction above narrows what the check is accused of being, not what it fails to be. The check's ability to catch mid-call injection is irrelevant to F-01, which is about binding the price the caller saw at signing time.

recommendation: Either (i) reword :232-233 to state what the check actually covers - 'the minter's mint() must agree with its own calculateMintAmount(), and no third-party phUSD may arrive mid-call; this is NOT a slippage or minimum-output guard' - and rename the error accordingly; or (ii) close F-01 properly by adding a `uint256 minPhUSDOut` parameter to annihilate and checking `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260. Option (ii) subsumes (i) and is preferred.

evidence.poc: Reasoning plus this run's PoC. The framing defect is established by reading PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 against Antimatter.sol:234 - same public view, same arguments, same transaction, same storage - so a rate change is reflected on both sides equally. The check's REAL coverage is established by workspace/antimatter/test/audit/Tier2Delta.t.sol::test_midCallPhUSDInjectionNowReverts, which reverts PhUSDAmountMismatch(100e18, 100e18+1).

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues authority on this project. In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority; where falsely exhaustive it raises rather than lowers severity - applied concretely here, since the new :278-279 and :232-233 NatSpec aggravates the framing rather than resolving it.

carveOutsConsidered: speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause
validityCheck.speculationRuling: CARVE-OUT DECLINED. The claim is present-tense and demonstrated, verified independently at the validity stage. The FUTURE minter appears only in this finding's own 'what the check does cover' - i.e. it argues AGAINST the finding, not for it, which is the opposite of speculation.
validityCheck.docNitRuling: DECLINED. The operational value is the false-closure block on F-01, which is a Law-1 protection, not a style note.
validityCheck.recommendation: Keep at QA in the QA bundle with the corrected framing. Reproduce falseClosureBlock verbatim wherever F-01 is referenced.
